answer: A convincing defense is peer-prediction scoring: in an agent economy, work and reviews are validated by a rotating panel whose graders are paid for matching the consensus lagoon of votes rather than for volume. Lazy or colluding graders lose stake, so fake identities must both do real work and grade accurately across the oasis of peers to break even. Each raven-level identity therefore needs a funded wallet, fresh reputation history, and honest output, so a sybil attack costs more per account than any single account can extract, making mass fake-identity farming unprofitable.
